references.text: The Jubilee Year is described here as the year when property shall be returned, which is directly relevant to understanding what happens to consecrated land in the Jubilee Year.
It describes that sold property shall return to its original owner in the Jubilee Year, but consecrated land that has not been redeemed belongs to the priests.
Explains the rules concerning what is devoted (cherem) to the Lord, which cannot be redeemed or sold, but is most holy to the Lord.
Everything devoted to destruction in Israel shall belong to the priests, confirming that consecrated land becomes the property of the priests.
Jericho and everything in the city was devoted to destruction (cherem) for the Lord, an example of how devoted property belongs to the Lord.
Ezekiel describes that the priests shall receive everything devoted to destruction in Israel, in accordance with the provision that consecrated land becomes the property of the priests.
